What it means: Enrollment or prescription form returned without the prescriber's signature or attestation – the case cannot open.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): isn't signed | not signed | didn't sign | missing signature | signature line | attestation | needs the doctor's signature
Example line from demo calls: "…the prescriber attestation on page two isn't signed."

What it means: Copy of the insurance card (front and back) not received, so benefits cannot be verified.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): insurance card | front and back | card copy | copy of the card | never attached | didn't get a copy | card was never
Example line from demo calls: "…we didn't get a copy of her insurance card, front and back…"

What it means: Pages missing or blank in a fax; office believes it was sent.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): fax confirmation | only shows | pages | came through blank | didn't go through | didn't go | we sent everything | thought we scanned
Example line from demo calls: "…the fax confirmation only shows three pages, so it probably didn't go."

What it means: Weight, diagnosis code, prescriber NPI, dose or other required field left blank.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): weight | diagnosis code | ICD | NPI | N P I | dose | prescription section | blank
Example line from demo calls: "We need Ava's current weight… the diagnosis code…"

What it means: Consent or authorization page not signed by the patient or caregiver.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): consent page | consent form | wasn't signed by | caregiver | mom can sign | HIPAA authorization
Example line from demo calls: "…the caregiver consent page wasn't signed by her mom."

What it means: The person who handles forms is out, busy or unreachable – a common cause of delay.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): is out | out this week | out sick | at a conference | not at her desk | not picking up | swamped | short today | short-staffed | covering two jobs | only Karen does
Example line from demo calls: "Karen is the nurse who handles all the specialty enrollment forms, and she's actually out this week."

What it means: Agent is calling again about the same open item.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): calling again | second call | third call | following up | my second | still waiting | still need | again about
Example line from demo calls: "This is actually my second call on Mister Nguyen."

What it means: Agent or office commits to an action by a date – must be tracked to see if it is kept.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): I'll call back | I'll check | I'll follow up | first thing Monday | by Friday | this afternoon | by end of day | I'll send | I'll fax | I'll let her know
Example line from demo calls: "I'll put a reminder to call back Monday afternoon if we haven't received it."
Demo call(s): ST01, ST02, ST03, ST05, DR01, DR03

What it means: Office admits a backlog or process problem affecting many patients.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): that's on us | pile up | in her queue | backlog | behind on | covering two jobs | two weeks?
Example line from demo calls: "Karen has been covering two jobs… the specialty forms just pile up when she's out."

What it means: Call ends in voicemail or no answer; outreach is not landing.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): leave a message | voicemail | can't come to the phone | away from my desk | no answer | third attempt | haven't been able to reach
Example line from demo calls: "This is our third attempt to reach you…"

What it means: Caller is put on hold or transferred – adds time and drop risk.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): can you hold | please hold | thanks for holding | let me transfer | transfer you | let me see if she's
Example line from demo calls: "Can you hold please?"

Signal: Payer requires letter of medical necessity
What it means: Payer states an LMN is required for the prior authorization.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): letter of medical necessity | LMN | medical necessity letter | necessity letter
Example line from demo calls: "First, a letter of medical necessity signed by Doctor Kim."

What it means: Payer lists clinical documents or criteria: notes, labs, ALP, ursodiol history, step therapy, genetic test.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): clinic notes | chart notes | clinical notes | labs | A L P | ALP | ursodiol | UDCA | twelve months | step therapy | genetic test | itching documented | criteria
Example line from demo calls: "…liver labs from the last three months that show his ALP, plus documentation that he's been on ursodiol for at least twelve months."

What it means: Drug is covered but needs a prior authorization – sets the next step.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): covered | needs a prior authorization | requires prior auth | PA required | covered with a prior
Example line from demo calls: "It's covered with a prior authorization."

Signal: PA pended or denied for missing documents
What it means: PA put on hold or denied because documents were missing or incomplete.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): pended | pending | on hold | denied | missing | incomplete | resubmit | send it again | not received
Example line from demo calls: "…the prior auth was pended. They're saying it's missing a letter of medical necessity…"

What it means: What the payer asked for (S12/S13) differs from what the office was told on a later call.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): Rule, not keywords: S12 or S13 in payer call AND office call for same case lists fewer items (e.g. 'just the notes', 'notes and labs') or omits the LMN
Example line from demo calls: Payer: "…and a letter of medical necessity." → Agent to office: "Just the latest clinical notes and labs."

What it means: Agent describes requirements loosely instead of naming each document.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): that kind of stuff | the usual | whatever the doctor usually sends | something like | I think they | probably on their website | some clinical documentation
Example line from demo calls: "…notes, labs, that kind of stuff…"

What it means: Office says nobody told them about a needed document – evidence of an earlier communication gap.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): nobody told us | we sent what you said | didn't know | first I'm hearing | wasn't asked for
Example line from demo calls: "Nobody told us about a letter. We sent what you said, notes and labs."

What it means: Agent recaps the specific documents the payer needs before ending the call.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): to recap | just to recap | so to recap | one, | two, | three, | so that's | all of it to
Example line from demo calls: "So just to recap before I let you go: one, the signed letter of medical necessity; two…"

What it means: Agent agrees a specific date with the office for submission.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): can you get that submitted by | can you send it by | by Thursday | by Friday | does that work | doable | works for
Example line from demo calls: "Can you get that submitted by Thursday, March fourth?" – "Thursday works."

What it means: Agent commits to check back on a specific day.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): I'll call you Friday | I'll check in | I'll call to confirm | following up like I promised
Example line from demo calls: "I'll call you Friday morning to confirm it went through."

What it means: Call ends with a generic line and no document list, date or owner.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): let us know if you need anything | let me know if you need anything | they'll let you know | you can probably find it
Example line from demo calls: "Alright, well, let us know if you need anything."

What it means: Patient worries about out-of-pocket cost or affording therapy.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): how much | out of pocket | deductible | a lot for us | can't afford | can't pay | keep paying | expensive | copay | owe
Example line from demo calls: "…even a few hundred a month is a lot for us right now."
Demo call(s): DR01; journey ('Nobody told me I'd owe $1,200')

What it means: Change in income or employment raises drop-off risk.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): out of work | lost my job | laid off | income | money is tight
Example line from demo calls: "My husband's been out of work since December."

What it means: Travel, distance, transport or time off work makes therapy hard to start or continue.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): hours from me | three hours | each way | drive | driving | one car | day off work | don't drive | too far | lab visits
Example line from demo calls: "Lakeview is about three hours from me, each way."
Demo call(s): DR02; journey ('lab visits two hours away')

What it means: Patient is unsure about starting: ambivalence, needs time, defers to family.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): need to think about it | think it over | talk to my husband | talk to my wife | not sure | I don't know | not ready
Example line from demo calls: "I need to think about it. Let me talk to my husband first."

What it means: Patient declines to schedule, transfer or proceed.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): call me later | not ready to schedule | not today | I'll call them | maybe later | hold off
Example line from demo calls: "Can they just call me later? I'm not ready to schedule anything today."

What it means: Copay / assistance application started but not finished or sent.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): started it | haven't finished | didn't send | still need to fill | application
Example line from demo calls: "I started it. I haven't finished it yet."

What it means: Repeated failed contact; referral may be closed – patient never starts.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): third attempt | haven't heard back | close the referral | unable to reach | no response
Example line from demo calls: "If we don't hear from you within ten days, we may have to close the referral."

What it means: A support offer is made – copay program, bridge / quick-start supply, travel help, local lab. Absence after S23–S26 is a missed opportunity.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): copay program | assistance program | bridge supply | quick start | free trial | travel assistance | travel support | local lab | closer to you | foundation
Example line from demo calls: "…you're eligible for our copay program…" · "I can ask… whether your labs can be done at a lab near you."

What it means: Patient says they may stop or want to stop therapy.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): thinking of stopping | should I stop | want to stop | give up | not worth it | quit
Example line from demo calls: "…honestly, I'm thinking of stopping."

What it means: Patient describes taking the drug in a way that conflicts with the label, e.g. with a bile acid binding resin.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): with my cholestyramine | at the same time as | bile acid | colestipol | take it with | double dose | skip
Example line from demo calls: "I take it with my cholestyramine every morning."

What it means: Symptom or side effect mentioned after starting therapy – must go to human safety review.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): side effect | itching is worse | rash | diarrhea | stomach | vomiting | since I started | after my first dose | reaction | hospital
Example line from demo calls: "The itching is worse since I started – should I stop?"

What it means: Question about use outside the label or a medical question the hub cannot answer.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): is it okay for | can I take it while | pregnant | my other child | younger than | dose for
Example line from demo calls: "Can I take it with cholestyramine?"

What it means: Caller expresses frustration, waiting or having to repeat information.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): nobody tells me | still waiting | I already | again? | two weeks? | so sorry | ugh
Example line from demo calls: "Two weeks? Oh no. I'm so sorry."

What it means: Caller expresses relief or satisfaction – evidence an action worked.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): that was fast | that helps | perfect | that would really help | great, thank you
Example line from demo calls: "Great, that was fast."

What it means: Agent confirms patient identity (name + date of birth) before discussing details.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): date of birth | confirm your date of birth | can you confirm
Example line from demo calls: "Can you confirm your date of birth for me?"

What it means: Same office makes the same mistake across patients – target for Field Access education.
Keywords & phrases (pipe-separated): fifth patient | second patient this week | other patients from your office | all held up | same thing
Example line from demo calls: "…Noah is the fifth patient from your office this month where we're waiting on something."
